title: fix(spec,core): ADR-0049 tombstones name the npm release that carries the removal, and a gate keeps them there
body:
Fixes #18048

Clause-②: no

ADR-0049 tombstones, refusal strings and doc pages across fifteen files dated a removal to the next npm major of `@objectstack/spec` — a bare **18** attached to the package name. There is no npm 18, and under ADR-0087's level ruling (Amended 2026-09-13) there will not be one as the carrier: *"A tombstone names the npm release it ships in, ⛔ never the protocol major […] a retirement shipping `minor` lands in `17.x.y`"*. A sibling repository had already hung a cleanup schedule on "the PR that pushes the spec package to its next major" — an event that will never come.

This is the class's **second** appearance. Ten sites of it were corrected by hand in July with no gate, and that card closed `completed`. So the prose fix is half of this PR; the other half is `pnpm check:future-spec-major`.

## What replaces the bad number, and why it is two answers

Determined **per site** from `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, never pasted. The sites split cleanly, and the two halves take different spellings because different things are known about them.

**Already shipped ⇒ the release that actually carries it — `17.3.0`** (published on npm; `npm view @objectstack/spec versions` ends `…17.2.0, 17.3.0, 17.4.0`). Eighteen hand sites plus four generated rows:

| retirement | changeset in `CHANGELOG.md` | release |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PluginHealthCheck.autoRestart` / `maxRestartAttempts` / `restartBackoff` | `b72db01` | `17.3.0` |
| `HotReloadConfig.stateStrategy: 'disk'`/`'distributed'`, `distributedConfig` | `4635f3e` | `17.3.0` |
| `HotReloadConfig.watchPatterns` | `ee3595c` | `17.3.0` |
| form-view `options[].default` | `c459da6` | `17.3.0` |

This is the version an upgrading reader greps in `CHANGELOG.md` after the tombstone error, which is exactly what the changeset-to-CHANGELOG contract exists to make findable.

**Not shipped yet ⇒ the bare published major, `17`.** Eleven hand sites plus three generated rows, covering three removals that are still unreleased changesets on this branch:

| retirement | pending changeset |
|:--|:--|
| the seven cron-typed positions (export schedules, `ScheduleState.cronExpression`, `DataSyncConfig.schedule`, `CacheWarmup.schedule`, backup / DR-test schedules) | `.changeset/cron-typed-positions-retired.md` |
| `CacheWarmup.strategy: 'scheduled'` | `.changeset/17157-cache-warmup-scheduled-strategy-retired.md` |
| `PluginStartupResult.startTime` / `plugin` / `health` | `.changeset/16059-startup-orchestrator-shipped-shape.md` |

For these the carrier minor is **unknown at authoring time**, so any digit is a guess — the same guess that produced this defect. Bare `17` is the one spelling that is true, exists, and cannot go stale:

1. **It asserts exactly what is known.** Each of those three changesets declares `minor`, and ADR-0087 guarantees a pre-GA retirement ships `minor`, so the carrier is necessarily some `17.x.y`. The major is a fact; the minor is not.
2. **It names a version that exists.** Bare `17` is the published major.
3. **It is the house form.** 588 bare-`17` citations sit in the tree, measured with this PR's own matcher.
4. **It is what the ledger prescribes.** `docs/v17-docs-sweep.md` run 3 fixed "17 passages dating v17 removals to 18 → **17**" — bare, not a guessed minor — and that row is this class's detection fingerprint.
5. **It cannot seed a fourth recurrence.** A guessed `17.5.0` goes stale the moment the minor count moves; bare `17` does not.
6. **The neighbours already read that way.** `startup-orchestrator.zod.ts`'s own surviving `duration` → `durationMs` tombstone says bare `@objectstack/spec 17`, three lines from the three this PR rewrites.

⛔ **No protocol-major reference is altered.** `toMajor: 18`, `step18` and the `PROTOCOL_VERSION` ladder are correct and untouched — nothing here matches a number that is not directly attached to the package name, so "retired in protocol major 18" is out of reach by construction. Untouched-control: `git grep -c 'toMajor: 18'` and `git grep -c 'step18'` read the same before and after.

## The gate — `pnpm check:future-spec-major`

`scripts/check-future-spec-major.mjs`, registered in the root `package.json` and wired into `lint.yml` (the gate step and the `--self-test` invocation `check:self-test-wired` requires; that gate reads 0 findings over 223 scripts).

**The class is derived at runtime**, never hardcoded: "an `@objectstack/spec` version whose major is above the major in `packages/spec/package.json`". A gate hardcoding the literal goes dormant the day the tree reaches that major, and the next stale tombstone will name the one after.

**It joins the joints before matching**, because a single-line matcher reads a false zero on live sites. `packages/core/src/health-monitor.ts` splits the phrase as `"… in @objectstack/spec " + '18 (#12032, …'`; there are JSDoc `*` continuations and plain wraps too. **And it reads the backticked package name** — `` `@objectstack/spec` 18 `` in the same file and in `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` — which is a second, independent way to read zero.

**The gap is bounded to a sentence continuation.** Exactly one space on the same line, or a line break crossed through recognised joint syntax (a closing quote, a `+`, a JSDoc `*`, indentation). A run of two or more spaces or a tab is column alignment, never prose, so `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs`'s `@objectstack/spec   414 files   496.4s` is not a finding. That bound has its own self-test fixture, carrying that row verbatim.

**Two exemption mechanisms, and neither is a path allowlist.** Three sites cite the bad number in order to forbid it, and a gate that cannot tell a tombstone from a quotation of a bad tombstone reds on the ruling that forbids the bug.

- **R1, structural.** A citation wholly inside a Markdown **double**-backtick code span is the phrase quoted as a PATTERN, which is what a fingerprint row is — so `docs/v17-docs-sweep.md`'s table row needs no ledger entry, and neither will the next fingerprint row. A **single**-backtick span is not exempt; that is the live tombstone form.
- **R2, a witnessed self-invalidating ledger.** Each entry names a file, the major it excuses, a `witness` regex that must still match the quoting sentence, a pinned `covers` count, and a written `why` the failure text prints. A path allowlist says "this file may say anything"; this says "this file may say exactly this, and must still say it". Three refusals follow, each with its own battery: a **new** citation in an exempt file matches no witness and reds; a witness that matches nothing reds (editing the quotation away kills its exemption instead of leaving a hole); a `covers` count that moves reds.

**The detector is excluded from its own corpus** — it documents the class in its header and holds the adversarial fixtures in its self-test, so it cites the bad form by necessity. ⛔ That would be a hole, so it comes with a compensating control in the opposite direction: the file MUST still carry at least `SELF_FIXTURE_FLOOR` citations above the published major. Gut the fixtures — the one edit the exclusion would otherwise hide — and the gate reds on itself.

**The self-test is the only instrument watching the rule**, because this gate's defect class *is* its matching rule: green means the finding set is empty, weakening can only shrink that set, and the empty set is the fixed point of shrinking. 29 batteries with a pinned roster, a floor and the module-flag handshake, including the wrapped fixture, the backticked fixture, a fenced-code fixture, the column-aligned bound, a legitimate bare-17 fixture that must pass, a derived-class fixture (the same corpus goes green once the manifest says 18), and an empty-corpus refusal.

## Census, under the gate's own instrument

Re-runnable at this head:

```
node scripts/check-future-spec-major.mjs --census
```

| reading | before (`34545d6c6c`) | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| live sites above the published major | 39 / 17 files | **0** |
| bare `18` remaining (all exempt quotations) | 39 / 17 files | 3 / 2 files |
| bare `17` control | 588 / 174 files | 602 / 176 files |
| dotted `17.x` control | 489 / 106 files | 511 / 113 files |

The bare-17 control moving is the fix landing, not over-matching: fourteen of this PR's rewrites add a bare-`17` citation, and the dotted bucket gains the twenty-two that now say `17.3.0`. Over an unchanged file the matcher's verdict does not move.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — 511 files / 14933 tests pass. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core test` — 51 files / 1321 tests pass. Both matter here: `health-monitor.test.ts` and `hot-reload.test.ts` pin those guidance strings **by content**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec --filter @objectstack/core typecheck` — green.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — all 15 generated artifacts up to date; `check:docs` green. The seven sites in `content/docs/references/kernel/{plugin-lifecycle-advanced,startup-orchestrator}.mdx` were **regenerated**, never hand-edited: the zod docblocks and `retiredKey()` prescriptions moved and `gen:docs` projected them.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` — 151 derived families accounted for, 148 run, 3 NOT MEASURED, 0 unrun. The three are named in the report: two exit 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, both needing a whole-tree `pnpm build`) and `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, whose own self-test is a recorded 597 s in `lint.yml` against this container's ~600 s foreground cap.
- **ESLint, narrowed and the narrowing proved.** Population read from eslint's own config: 6992 tracked files with lintable extensions, none globally ignored per its `isPathIgnored`. Linted: 12 files, the count read from `--format json`, 0 errors / 0 warnings. Invariance: `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting for any file — zero `parserOptions.project` and zero `projectService` in it, which its own header states and measured with a positive control — so every verdict depends only on that file's bytes plus the shared config. This PR changes neither the config nor a byte of the other 6980 files, so no untouched file's verdict can move. Quoted from `68ff8a1082`.

## Clause-②, measured rather than argued

Every affected string is a docblock, a doc page, or a `retiredKey()` / `guidance` **message**. The key is refused before and after, so no accept/reject result moves for any input. The control that decides it: the phrase has **0 hits** across `packages/*/api-surface` and `packages/*/export-origins`, so no published declaration baseline carries these sentences and none moves. `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` is green; the `--pair` C6 row is in the report.

Changeset grades `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/core`, both `patch`. `packages/core` is in scope although the card is anchored `domain:spec`: the triage ruling makes the gate tree-wide, and a tree-wide gate cannot be green on `main` while 11 live sites remain in `packages/core` — six of them runtime refusal strings an operator reads.

## Acceptance notes

- **One bounded in-place fix, declared.** `packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts` carried a docblock reading "the watch-placeholder key retired in **18**" — the same stale number, the same defect class, but with no package name attached, so it is outside the card's stated class and outside this gate's matcher by construction. It is now `17.3.0`, matching the prescription three lines below it that this PR also rewrites. Evidence: `git diff` on that file shows the two edits adjacent; the key's removal is `ee3595c` in the `17.3.0` section of `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Deliberately not changed.** `startup-orchestrator.zod.ts`'s `duration` → `durationMs` tombstone says bare `@objectstack/spec 17` for a rename that shipped in `17.4.0`. Bare `17` is correct and legitimate — less specific than it could be, not wrong — so it is not in this card's class and is left alone.
- **Two measurement readings are declared in the ledger, not rewritten.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/{registry.ts, entries/semantic/…}` record "controls objectstack 12966 and `@objectstack/spec` 4997 on the same corpus" and `docs/adr/0021-…md` records a `6526/6526` pass ratio. Those numbers are hit counts, not versions, and they sit exactly one space after the package name, so no whitespace rule can distinguish them from a citation. Rather than narrow the matcher — the move that produces a false zero — they carry witnessed `kind: 'measurement'` ledger entries.
- **Serial note.** #19598 (draft) touches `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` at hunks well clear of the site here, which is on line 2780. Re-derived on this branch after merging `origin/main`: no textual conflict.
